lines.en: [Main Scenario 95 has ended!]
After the scenario ended, the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal and the ‘Outer Gods’ gathered at the center of the Tongtian River for a victory feast.
[The Giant Story 「Journey to the West」 liberates the extras from their status.]
The Outer Gods who had been enslaved to the scenario under the oppression of the <Bureau> and <Emperor> were being freed.
【Oooooooooh】
【MonkeyKingMonkeyKingMonkeyKing】

Some of them had even followed the ‘Secretive Plotter’ before joining the scenario late. As the ‘Secretive Plotter’s’ Status weakened, they had naturally gone over to the Great Sage, Heaven's Equal, who had ascended as a new Outer God.
[Reward distribution will begin!]
The incarnations grinned from ear to ear at the rewards for Scenario 95 descending from the air.
Their joy was short-lived, however. Their eyes turned to a group of incarnations receiving staggering rewards.
“Wow, that's······.”
“I should've joined that Story chamber too······.”
It was the group from <Kim Dokja’s Company>. After individual rewards of a full million coins each, some were even receiving <Emperor>’s Star Relics.
Everything was being distributed according to procedure, so no one could object.
[The nebula <Emperor> protests to the Bureau about the scenario's fairness!]
No, there was someone. The hosts themselves, <Emperor>.
They had put so much into organizing a large-scale scenario, only for its rewards to pass wholesale to a small nebula. They could hardly help feeling wronged.
[The <Star Stream> dismisses <Emperor>’s protest.]
Just as some of <Emperor>’s constellations, unable to contain their anger, were about to unleash their Status, unexpected figures stopped them.
“Please stop. We lost.”
Fei Hu, <Emperor>’s strongest incarnation.
“What would the Myth-grade constellations think if they saw us now?”
<Emperor>’s Myth-grade constellations had not participated in this Journey to the West scenario. They were already watching all this from the final scenario.
“Conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of your honor.”
At the incarnation's firm words, even <Emperor>’s constellations belatedly flushed and lowered their heads.
Some distance away, Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye were watching.
“······That's unexpected.”
“It is.”
Most of the influential figures from great nebulae they had met so far had refused to admit defeat. This time was different.
Perhaps noticing their gazes, Fei Hu approached with a sheepish smile.
“Incarnation Jung Heewon.”
Jung Heewon tensed and gripped her steel sword. Fei Hu was one of the strongest opponents she had ever faced.
Fei Hu spoke gently.
“Incarnation Jung Heewon, that was a most impressive bout.”
“If the opportunity arises, I would very much like to invite you to China and share a meal.”
Looking closely, she could see a faint blush between his sideburns.
Watching this, Lee Jihye exclaimed through [Voice Transmission].
―······Wow, there are still people like this even as the world's ending.
Jung Heewon stared blankly at Fei Hu. He was hesitating, unable to meet her eyes.
Lee Jihye kept poking Jung Heewon in the side.
―Unnie, what are you doing? He's still the best of the men we've seen so far. He's nowhere near as handsome as my master, but······.
“I'm sorry, but.”
Jung Heewon replied as courteously as a murim master.
“I have pledged to spend my life with the sword.”
“As have I.”
“······Pardon?”
“I would dearly like to invite you to China and spend an entire night in profound swordplay with you.”

As Fei Hu rambled on, his eyes blazing, Jung Heewon felt a little overwhelmed. Glancing beside her, she found even Lee Jihye, who had been cheering her on with shining eyes, shaking her head. It would be a relief if all this was needless worry, but otherwise, trouble might be brewing.
Zzzzzzt······.
She heard her constellation sponsor stir, unable to watch any longer.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’······.]
‘It's fine, Uriel. Please stay out of it.’

If Uriel needlessly stepped in now, the embers of the dying war might flare up again. She would have liked to fight him one-on-one and beat him right then, but the surrounding constellations were watching······.
“I'm sorry, but I already······.”
This time, as she spoke, the steel sword in her hand trembled. The steel sword Lee Hyunsung had transformed into. Jung Heewon felt a wholly unreasonable resentment.
Why did this sword have to be a sword that couldn't even speak?
“What the hell? Move!”
It was Han Sooyoung who came to her rescue. Who knew when she had entered the scenario? She shoved past Fei Hu, looked around, and demanded,
“Where's Kim Dokja?”
······Kim Dokja?
Jung Heewon looked back at the man's incarnation body, which she had been carrying on her back all this time.
Fei Hu was looking displeased at Han Sooyoung's interruption. Looking between him and Kim Dokja's incarnation body, Jung Heewon had a brilliant idea.
“My lord!”
As though recalling the ‘Struggle for the Flag,’ Jung Heewon cradled Kim Dokja in her arms and cried out passionately.
“My lord, are you all right?”
Kim Dokja's pale incarnation body flopped limply in her arms.
“O King!”
Everyone was looking at Jung Heewon. Lee Jihye's mouth hung open, while Han Sooyoung looked incredulous.
And Fei Hu.
His expression said he finally understood everything.
“I see, Incarnation Jung Heewon. So that was how it was······?”

Fei Hu's gaze passed from Jung Heewon to Han Sooyoung, then to Lee Jihye, before settling on Kim Dokja's face. He bit his lip. Like an unfortunate extra envying the chosen protagonist, he slowly lowered his head, then slowly turned away.
Watching him go, Lee Jihye sent Jung Heewon a voice transmission.
―It's done, unnie. He's gone. Though I think he's got the wrong idea, which is annoying.
But Jung Heewon did not stop.
“My lord! Please wake up! My lord! If you don't wake up, I'll kill you!”
Slap! Slap! Slap! Slap!
Kim Dokja's left cheek began to swell under Jung Heewon's palm.
Han Sooyoung looked down at her with disdain and asked,
“······What are you doing?”
“Getting revenge.”
Han Sooyoung nodded in understanding, then took over from Jung Heewon, grabbing Kim Dokja by the collar and shaking him.
“Hey.”
“I told you I'd make you a new modifier. You couldn't wait even that long before getting yourself one?”
“Did you hear the narration I wrote? Did you hear the final passage? How was it? You can be honest, you bastard. You were moved, weren't you? Right?”
But Kim Dokja still did not answer. Frowning, Han Sooyoung kept slapping his other cheek, which had yet to swell.
Unable to bear the sight, Shin Yoosung ran over, pale with alarm.
“What on earth are you all doing!”
“Don't worry. He's breathing. He's not dead.”
Despite the commotion, Kim Dokja did not wake.
Opinions began to diverge among the group.
“He's definitely refusing to wake up on purpose. He knows what he's done.”
“True. Then maybe we should inflict some pain he can't bear······.”
“Aren't you all going too far?”
Five minutes passed, then ten, with no sign of consciousness. The group's expressions began to grow serious.
“······What's going on?”
Eventually, they found someone who could explain the situation for them.
Yoo Joonghyuk, who lay unconscious right beside Kim Dokja.
“Hey, Yoo Joonghyuk! Snap out of it! Why isn't that bastard Kim Dokja waking up?”
Slap! Slap! Slap! Slap!
Yoo Joonghyuk's firm cheeks did not swell as easily as Kim Dokja's. How much time passed like that? Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes opened to narrow slits.
“I am Yoo Joonghyuk······.”
“Damn it, what's wrong with this one now?”
Yoo Joonghyuk kept repeating the same words like someone out of his mind.
Yoo Sangah, who arrived belatedly, stopped Han Sooyoung.
“Stop badgering Joonghyuk-ssi. His memories are confused because of his Stories. He won't be in his right mind.”
“Sangah-unnie!”
Finally able to enjoy their reunion, the group gathered around Yoo Sangah.
Having reincarnated safely, Yoo Sangah radiated a grace different from before.
Watching this, Han Sooyoung gave a short laugh and asked,
“I heard you were the Descendant of Sakyamuni. You're not bald?”
“Religions are quite trendy these days.”
“Welcome back. You're a little late, though.”
“It wasn't easy getting here right as you were about to cause trouble.”
“······I'm not the one causing trouble. He is.”
Shrugging, Yoo Sangah reached toward the unconscious Kim Dokja. The ‘Golden Headband’ on his head shone with a brilliant golden light.
Jung Heewon nodded in satisfaction.
“You've got it on him properly. Now he can't run off anywhere.”
“······Unfortunately, it seems he already has.”
“What?”
“His soul body hasn't returned.”
A faint line extended toward the sky from the Golden Headband fastened around Kim Dokja. A line leading somewhere. Yoo Sangah spoke as she tried to make out where it ended.
“Don't worry. He hasn't gone far. And I don't think he left of his own accord.”
He had not left of his own accord. The meaning was clear.
Looking hurriedly around, Han Sooyoung asked,
“Where did the ‘Secretive Plotter’ go?”
The scenery in the dimensional passage was speeding past me.

Everything had happened in an instant. The moment I deactivated [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint], something seized my soul body. By the time I came to my senses, I was crossing a portal with the ‘Secretive Plotter.’
Normally, it would have been impossible. This case was rather special, however.
[You have failed to keep your ‘Existence Oath.’]
[Your soul body is temporarily bound by the Existence Oath contract.]
[Your contractor has ownership of your soul body for 24 hours.]
Looking at the messages in the air, I gave a hollow laugh.
―I didn't know you could use an [Existence Oath] like this.
[Existence Oath].
While the scenario was in progress, I was not to contact <Kim Dokja’s Company> and reveal my identity.
It was the only promise I had failed to keep properly in this scenario.
I had thought there was room for dispute, since the scenario's content had changed midway through. Apparently, the <Star Stream> had ruled that I had broken my oath.
―Are you going to kill me?

Intense sparks still flew from the entire body of the ‘Secretive Plotter,’ now in a boy's form. I could feel countless Yoo Joonghyuks watching me from within his Stories. They were not hostile Stories.
He clearly had no intention of killing me.
As Yoo Joonghyuk had said earlier, if he had intended to kill me, he had already had several opportunities.
Before long, the portal closed. We had arrived somewhere familiar to me. A forest thick with darkness.
The ‘Secretive Plotter’s’ home, ‘N'Gai's Forest.’
【Go in.】
With those words, my soul body was sucked into something.
I blinked, and my eyes moved. But I had neither arms nor legs. Wondering what on earth I had become, I looked around. My reflection appeared in the glass on the wall.
······I had become a small murim dumpling.
Apparently, this was the symbolic body [999] had used.
“How does it feel to be a dumpling!”
Who knew when they had appeared? The Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks ran up and mobbed me, kicking me with their feet. They were only Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks, so it did not hurt much.
Curling up to keep my dumpling wrapper from bursting, I shouted,
―I don't know what you're planning, but you can't stop me. I'll be back in my incarnation body after 24 hours anyway. If you want to kill me, shouldn't you do it now?
Of course, I did not say that because I actually wanted him to kill me.
I asked the ‘Secretive Plotter’ sitting on his throne,
―‘Secretive Plotter.’ What's your goal? Why on earth are you keeping me alive?
At my question, even the Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks stopped moving.
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ looked down at me. The strongest Outer God and constellation I knew. The strongest Yoo Joonghyuk of all Yoo Joonghyuks.
―I know you could have beaten us if you'd given it everything you had.
Even with Yoo Joonghyuk, who had recovered his memories of the 1864th round, joining forces with me, surpassing the ‘Secretive Plotter’ in the sheer Status of our Stories was impossible.
He was the sum of all history from the 0th round to the 1863rd, and a Yoo Joonghyuk who had endured an unfathomable span of time beyond even that.
Yet the ‘Secretive Plotter’ had chosen defeat over killing us.
“Because he needs you.”
The one who said that was [41], who had been listening.
“Because you're the human who has the final fragment of the ‘Final Wall.’”
Bihyung was terribly excited. Any dokkaebi who had personally witnessed the scenario unfolding on the screen before him would have been.
―Every time, I’ll do my best to fight back too.
The scenario completion message accompanied Kim Dokja's voice. Countless constellations' indirect messages erupted, and the entire <Star Stream> was shaking.
The new owner of the Giant Story 『Journey to the West』 had been decided.
‘He did it. That bastard Kim Dokja did it.’
A streamer had to remain impartial. But every referee had a team they secretly rooted for, and Bihyung was no different.
Like a parent looking at a grown child, Bihyung stroked the faces on the screen, looking deeply moved.
[Congratulations, Director Bihyung-nim.]
The subordinate dokkaebis around him offered their congratulations. They, too, knew that Bihyung had watched <Kim Dokja’s Company> for a long time.
[I knew they would do it too.]
[M-me too. Me too······!]
Some dokkaebis had even cheered for <Kim Dokja’s Company> alongside him. In fact, several looked every bit as flushed with excitement as Bihyung.
It was truly rare for dokkaebis, who pursued nothing but sensational material, to care so deeply about something.
[These kids are mine. Don't get any ideas.]
[Haha! Of course······.]
That was when urgent news arrived.
[Director-nim, Great Dokkaebi ‘Baram’······.]
[It's a promotion!]
······A promotion?
[Director Bihyung-nim, congratulations!]
[It looks like the Bureau's going to do its job properly for once!]
Amid the flood of messages, Bihyung could not get his bearings.
He was a ‘high-grade dokkaebi’ and the director of the Seoul branch. He had already risen as high as effort could take him.
To be promoted again from here meant······.
Surely, this was a good thing.
Why, then, did he have such an ominous feeling?
[The Great Dokkaebi is waiting.]
Guided by the low-grade dokkaebis, Bihyung entered a portal.
As the hazy mist cleared, he saw Great Dokkaebi Baram waiting in a gray passage.
[You've come, Bihyung.]
[Baram-nim.]
He patted Bihyung's shoulder as though acknowledging his hard work, then spoke.
[Congratulations. Your promotion has been decided.]
[······Pardon?]
[Do something about that vacant expression. Does it not feel real? A decision has been made to select you as the last ‘Great Dokkaebi.’]
Great Dokkaebi. The ultimate honor every streamer yearned for. Bihyung was dazed to see something he had only vaguely imagined become reality.
[······A Great Dokkaebi? Me?]
[Indeed. A promotion without precedent anywhere in the history of the <Star Stream>.]
Chuckling, Baram began to walk ahead.
Bihyung followed without knowing where they were going. He had so many questions.
Where on earth was this place, and······.
[Since you will soon become a Great Dokkaebi, surely it is time you met that person.]
Baram smiled as if he knew what Bihyung was thinking.
[By that person, you mean······.]
Even as he asked, Bihyung had an idea who it would be.
The air around them warped, and faint sparks seethed in the atmosphere. On closer inspection, every spark had the shape of a printed character. Something lay ahead. A being he had never seen before.
[We're here.]
Rounding the corridor and passing through the misty passage, they emerged into a vast hall.
No, could it be called a hall?
It was a chamber so immense its size could not even be measured. A broad wall stretched across it. That wall, too, was too wide to measure from beginning to end.
Printed characters seethed over the wall's surface, and cracks and patches of damage, large and small, marked it here and there.
Suddenly, Bihyung realized he had seen that wall somewhere before.
[······The Revelation Tablet?]
The Revelation Tablet. There was no mistaking it. Its shape was different, but the wall from which constellations received ‘revelations’ also had that appearance.
But why was the ‘Revelation Tablet’ here? And that size······.
[Everyone has gathered.]
The moment he heard the voice, Bihyung sank to the floor before he knew it. He had encountered countless constellations, but this time, he could not hide his tension.
He could not fathom the limits of the Status in that voice.
Looking beside him, he found every Great Dokkaebi, Baram included, prostrate and facing the front.
Someone stood before the ‘Revelation Tablet.’
Concealing his trembling, Bihyung slowly raised his head. Only then did he understand.
So that was it······ I see.
That being was the one absolute ruler who governed this <Bureau> and controlled the <Star Stream>.
The ‘King of Stories.’
Stroking the broken wall with long, white hands, the king slowly spoke.
[I will select ‘A Single Story’ to determine the next world.]
“I have the final fragment of the ‘Final Wall’?”
“That's right.”
I frowned at [41]’s voice.

I could roughly guess what he meant. The ‘Final Wall.’ Throughout this round, I had been gathering information about it. A subject never resolved even at the end of the original ‘Ways of Survival.’ I was convinced that this ‘wall’ would probably be the clue that determined how this round ended.
And the ‘final fragment’ these guys were talking about······.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates strongly!]
「Kim Dok ja」
Don't worry. I'll never hand you over to him.
Blinking slowly, I concentrated. The ‘Secretive Plotter’ was watching me. Though he had lost much of his Status, the being before me was still the strongest constellation and ‘Outer God’ I knew.
Recalling the day I first came to ‘N'Gai's Forest,’ I spoke.
“You said something before. That when ‘Sacred Three-Question Exchange’ ended, I had to figure out why I'd come here.”
【Indeed.】
“You actually want to see the end of this world. Don't you? Whatever you say, you're placing your hopes in this worldline too.”
The ‘Secretive Plotter’s’ eyebrows twitched faintly.
However much he denied being Yoo Joonghyuk, he could not even discard Yoo Joonghyuk's habits.
“And you need my [Fourth Wall] for that. That's why you've kept me alive all this time. Am I right?”
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ did not answer.
If that was how he wanted to play it, I had an idea too.
Zzzzzzt.
“I never got to hear the last answer in the ‘Three-Question Exchange’ back then.”
[‘Sacred Three-Question Exchange’ resumes!]
[You have one question remaining.]
Back then, I had asked the ‘Secretive Plotter.’
『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.
―Secretive Plotter. Do you know the epilogue of that novel?
“Secretive Plotter. What exactly was the ‘ending’ you saw?”

The ‘Ways of Survival’ I had read ended at chapter 3149. But even though I had not seen it, the ‘Secretive Plotter’ had lived beyond that point. He had survived that unrecorded time and reached his own ending.
What on earth had he seen there?
What had he seen that made him become an ‘Outer God’ and appear in this worldline?
[41] was the first to react to my question. Looking a little angry, he shouted at me.
“That question is······!”
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ stopped him, and all the other Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks fell silent.
Yoo Joonghyuk in a boy's form. The ‘Secretive Plotter’ was looking at me.
Suddenly, it felt strange. Nowhere in ‘Ways of Survival’ was Yoo Joonghyuk's boyhood properly depicted. It was only occasionally described through recollections.
But not being depicted did not mean it had never existed.
It was like chapter 3150 of ‘Ways of Survival.’ Somewhere I did not know, Yoo Joonghyuk had been born and survived. And he had become the protagonist of ‘Ways of Survival.’
【Up to what point does the book you read recount my actions?】
The protagonist with the unfamiliar face was asking me.
After a brief hesitation, I answered.
“······Up until the moment you go to the Dokkaebi King.”
I recalled the final scene of ‘Ways of Survival.’

The journey to kill the Dokkaebi King. As Yoo Joonghyuk made his way through the ‘Final Mist,’ his story entered its last phase. There was no explanation at all of what happened afterward, or what he saw after that.
That was why I had been bewildered while reading the installment back then. I had been afraid it might actually be an open ending.
【What did I look like at the last moment?】
The unexpected question caught me off guard.
I had never imagined he would ask these things.
“Why do you······.”
【Did I look successful? Did it seem as if I could achieve my goal at the end?】
The moment I heard that, an inexplicable tightness gripped my chest.
I did not know why the ‘Secretive Plotter’ was asking me such a question.
Whatever answer I gave, those events had all already happened to the ‘Secretive Plotter.’
My impressions did not matter in the least. Not in the least······.
······Did they really not matter?
I barely managed to move my lips.
I was not ready to answer this question. But ready or not, I had to answer.
「At that moment, she realized that the world had passed entirely out of her hands.」
Memories of [Peace Land] came back. The expression on manga artist Asuka Ren's face as she let her world go. The responsibility of someone who had created a world.
I was not the author who had created ‘Ways of Survival,’ as she had created hers. But I.
「After all, it’s entirely thanks to you that this story could come into the world, dear reader.」
Was the person who had watched that story to the end.
“You succeeded. Because you did your best.”
Giving this answer was the duty of the person who had watched that story to the end.
Slowly, faithfully, I recalled every sentence I remembered.
“It was the same in every round. You always made the best choice. I don't know what ending you reached, but it wasn't wrong.”
All of Yoo Joonghyuk's rounds flashed through my mind.
What Yoo Joonghyuk had gained, and what he had lost.
“Your companions would think so too.”
Even the sight of his back as he reached the final chapter, left all alone.
Did I have the right to say this?
I did not know.
“For some reason, you didn't look very happy at the end.”
Even now, the scene I had read would not leave my mind.
「At last, Yoo Joonghyuk, who had lost everything, looked at the mist. The empty answer he had sought lay beyond that mist.」
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ faced me with exactly the expression described in that scene.
【I see.】
“······Why did you suddenly ask that?”
【I was curious. You alone saw it from beginning to end.】
I could say nothing.
【I was curious about the meaning someone other than myself had given my life. That is all.】
The ‘Secretive Plotter’s’ words were as hollow as those of a being who had lost all meaning. As if to resist that emptiness, I spoke.
“······Your life saved someone.”
To someone who had lost so much, saving a boy whose name he did not even know would offer no comfort. That boy had no connection to him. He was neither his companion nor his family.
My lips moved several times, but I could say nothing.
The life I had lived was of no help at all in saving him.
Watching me, the ‘Secretive Plotter’ spoke.
【When I first saw you, I thought I should take you in.】
Take me in. Suddenly, I recalled the moment I had first met him.
<Sponsor (背後) Selection>
―Choose your sponsor.
―Your chosen sponsor will become a dependable supporter.
1. Abyssal Black Flame Dragon
2. Demon-like Judge of Fire
3. Secretive Plotter
4. Prisoner of the Golden Headband
······I remembered.
Yes, that was how it had been. The ‘Secretive Plotter’ was the third option in my first Sponsor Selection. Back then, he had tried to become my constellation sponsor.
【I continued watching this worldline afterward. There were times I was surprised. That surprise surprised me. I had not been surprised in a very long time.】

I knew it too. As this worldline's story unfolded, the ‘Secretive Plotter’ had watched us, sending all kinds of indirect messages. Even now, I could search the message log and read the ones he had sent.
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is intrigued by your choice.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ marvels at your talent for being a sucker.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is disappointed by your rash declaration.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ has a gleam in its eyes at your plan.]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ is curious about your strategy.]
That was why meeting him in person for the first time had felt so unfamiliar.
Now, of course, I knew those indirect messages had been written on his behalf by [666] and the other Yoo Joonghyuks······.
【I had to decide. Whether to watch this twisted world, or destroy it.】
“······Is that why you sent me to the 1863rd round?”
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ nodded.
His choice had, in turn, become the beginning of this ‘worldline.’
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ continued.

【It was for a similar reason that I gave this round's Yoo Joonghyuk information about the 1863rd round. I needed to test which of you was better suited to seeing the ending. You, or this round's Yoo Joonghyuk.】
“So what's your verdict?”
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ looked down at me without answering.
【At the end of this world is an immense wall. The ‘Final Wall,’ which can only be opened once every key has been gathered.】
―You have received answers to all your questions.
―‘Sacred Three-Question Exchange’ ends.
Suddenly, I understood.
His words just now had been the answer to my ‘Three Questions.’

The sparks circling the ‘Secretive Plotter’ intensified. Some information consumed a great deal of probability merely by being spoken. If it concerned the end of this world, it was only natural that the price in probability would be high.
The ‘Final Wall.’
That was the ending the ‘Secretive Plotter’ had encountered in his epilogue.
【The ‘fragment’ you possess is the final key I have been seeking.】
I drew back nervously. Being in the form of a [Murim Dumpling] made moving backward difficult, but I had to put some distance between us somehow.
If my [Fourth Wall] was the ‘Secretive Plotter’s’ objective, then he······.
The way the ‘Secretive Plotter’ slowly opened and closed his hand was strangely frightening.
The other Kkoma Yoo Joonghyuks, too, were looking up at him with tense eyes.
【This worldline was made by twisting too many things. I cannot judge whether leaving you be is right or wrong.】
A twisted worldline. Broken probability.
I had heard it countless times already.
“So what are you going to do?”
I threw out whatever came to mind. What mattered was buying time. Somehow, I had to stall until I could return to my original body.

“I don't really understand what you're saying. All that complicated stuff about the result devouring the cause or whatever—I don't get it. But whatever the case, my companions and I fought with everything we had to get this far. The ending's right in front of us now.”
Now, I could see it.
The ending of the story that had never been written down.
【Seeing an ending is not everything. What matters is making the right ending.】
“The right ending? The one who decides that······.”
【A story with twisted probability will ultimately create a calamity.】
Those words, the sort a dokkaebi might say, left me briefly stunned.
“That doesn't sound like you. You haven't even seen it yet―”
That was when an earthquake struck. Something fell with a crash.
The wineglasses on the round table toppled and spilled. The entire forest was shaking.
This was certainly no natural earthquake.
The ‘Secretive Plotter’ slowly rose from his throne and passed me. His empty eyes took in the forest.
‘N'Gai's Forest,’ engulfed in a raging inferno.
His forest was burning.
【Aaaaaaaah】
【SaveMeSaveMeSaveMeSaveMeSaveMe】

Trees that had towered toward the sky burned, scattering ash. The ‘Outer Gods’ hiding in the forest screamed. The tremendous heat was rapidly raising the temperature in the hall. This was no simple act of arson.
Even I could feel it.
Someone—a being with immense Status—was attacking this place.
But who on earth?
It was impossible. This was the sanctuary of none other than the ‘Secretive Plotter.’ Who would dare invade it?
Could it be a great nebula's doing?
<Vedas>? <Olympus>? Or······ <Asgard>?
I tried recalling constellations associated with ‘fire.’ No modifier readily came to mind, however.
Heat burning the whole vast forest.
······Had there been another being in the original novel with this much power?
【OKingOKingOKing】
【GetAwayGetAwayGetAwayGetAwayGetAwayGetAwayGetAway】
Small ‘Outer Gods’ crowded around the ‘Secretive Plotter.’ Many ‘Outer Gods’ had left him, but many still remained. Like subjects foreseeing their kingdom's fall, they protected their king.
Looking down at his subjects, the ‘Secretive Plotter’ spoke to me.
【Demon King of Salvation. I, too, once made the same mistake as you.】
Despite the urgency of the burning forest, his voice was calm.
As though he had foreseen all of this.
【Foolishly, I tried to change a past that was already set.】
